source.author: lucan
source.text: Saepe etiam caris cognato in funere dira Thessalis incubuit membris: atque oscula figens, Truncavitque caput, compressaque dentibus ora Laxavit: siccoque haerentem gutture linguam Praemordens, gelidis infudit murmura labris, Arcanumque nefas Stygias mandavit ad umbras.
source.text_original: Saepe etiam caris cognato in funere dira / Thessalis incubuit membris: atque oscula figens, / Truncavitque caput, compressaque dentibus ora / Laxavit: siccoque haerentem gutture linguam / Praemordens, gelidis infudit murmura labris, / Arcanumque nefas Stygias mandavit ad umbras.
source.text_english: Often too on a kinsman’s funeral pyre the Thessalian woman has lain upon dear limbs in dreadful embrace; and, planting kisses, she has severed the head and, with the mouth crushed beneath her teeth, has loosened it; and biting through the tongue clinging in the dry throat, she has poured mutterings into the cold lips and entrusted the secret crime to Stygian shades.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: tum, vobis siquod inausum arcanumque nefas et adhuc incondita leti sors superest, date fallaci pudibunda senectae exitia indecoresque obitus.
reuse.text_original: tum, vobis siquod inausum / arcanumque nefas et adhuc incondita leti / sors superest, date fallaci pudibunda senectae / exitia indecoresque obitus.
reuse.text_english: then, if for you there remains any forbidden deed, unattempted and secret, and any still unshaped doom of death, grant shameful ends from a deceiving old age and dishonorable deaths.
